players.product: vacuum pumps and exhaust abatement systems for semiconductor fabs (Vacuum Technique business area)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 (President Vagner Rego): record order intake of SEK 52.3 billion, organic growth 25% (3% structural, total 29%), with all four business areas growing organically and three at double digits: Compressor Technique 6%, Vacuum Technique 82%, Power Technique 13%, Industrial Technique 12%; record revenues of SEK 47.9 billion, organic +11%; margin 20.8%, underlying 21.3% after Industrial Technique restructuring. Orders by region: Asia +39% (mainly Vacuum Technique), North America +39%, Europe +8%, Africa and Middle East +21%, South America +4%. Four acquisitions closed in the quarter. CFO Peter Kinnart: effective tax rate 21% helped by tax credits.
quarterly_data.figure: orders SEK 52.3 billion (organic +25%); Vacuum Technique orders +82% organic; revenues SEK 47.9 billion (organic +11%)

quarterly_data.signal: Vacuum Technique (Vagner Rego / CFO Peter Kinnart): orders +82% organic on 'fantastic development on the semiconductor market' plus industrial and scientific vacuum (space, R&D, metallurgy, battery production); revenue +28% organic; margin 22.2%, with capacity ramp-up costs still weighing. In Genesee, U.S., spare-parts production started gradually in Q3 and assembly of pumps is to start in Q4, so the site is not yet at full capacity. Rego: there was 'a little bit more pre-ordering this quarter' by key OEM accounts securing production slots, and with semi customers 'the biggest discussions... is output'; he said Atlas Copco has 'the highest capacity of dry vacuum pump production' and is prepared to add more. Lead times are typically three to six months but 'might be a little bit longer' given the pipeline. Demand mixes populating fabs built last year with process tools and new fab announcements and new players.
quarterly_data.figure: Vacuum Technique orders +82% organic, revenue +28% organic, margin 22.2%; lead times typically 3 to 6 months

quarterly_data.signal: Vacuum Technique pricing and margin (CFO Peter Kinnart): the semiconductor segment remains an 'extremely concentrated market segment with very strong purchasing power from the big players', so pricing gains are 'not as evident' as the strong market suggests; Rego: customer agreements expire on different dates, so better price levels come 'step by step'. Kinnart expects 'some level of margin expansion' to continue but not as large as in the last two quarters. To stay agile in a downturn Atlas Copco now avoids long commitments on subcontracted machining, paying somewhat more short term.

Compressor Technique (Vagner Rego / CFO Peter Kinnart): orders +6% organic and revenue +5% organic; operating margin 23.6%, hit by currency (notably the Korean won), product and geographic mix and higher supply-chain costs - Kinnart tied commodity pressure to data centers being built 'all over the place' (oil price, aluminum castings, desiccant, electrical and electronic components); long-cycle projects with up to a year of lead time carry older prices. Gas and process: LNG demand mainly from the U.S.; no LNG orders from Korean shipyards this quarter while Chinese shipyards did well; a large heat-pump compressor order for district heating in Europe; CFO Kinnart called Q2's exceptional gas-and-process order intake 'probably the absolute record quarter'. Atlas Copco gained industrial-compressor market share in China. It closed the Euroklimat acquisition (cooling, low-temperature heat pumps), which will be dilutive.

Industrial and Power Technique (Vagner Rego / CFO Peter Kinnart): Industrial Technique orders +12% organic (electronics, aerospace, defense; U.S. automotive customers needing flexible production lines; automation), revenue +2%, margin 18.7% (underlying 20.6%) after SEK 132 million restructuring of German product companies, helped by lower trade-tariff costs than last year. Power Technique orders +13% organic with record revenue and a margin of 18.3%, helped by the MTE acquisition and specialty rental; it launched the TwinPower dual generator. Kinnart expects an effective tax rate of about 22.5% in Q4 and a currency effect of about plus half a billion SEK on the bottom line, all things being equal.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial Technique orders +12% organic; Power Technique orders +13% organic; Q4 tax rate about 22.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Near-term outlook on the call (President Vagner Rego): the sequential guidance refers to customer activity excluding large orders, FX swings and seasonality; he stressed there is seasonality between Q3 and Q4 and, with record orders received especially in semiconductors, 'it is hard to predict what is going to happen in the semi', while 'we continue to be very positive about the semi market'; for most other segments he believes activity will remain at the current level.
